adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for users without a TopicUser row, causing NoMethodError and a 500 on unsubscribe; should use TopicUser.change (upsert) or handle the missing record

Unsubscribe link is a state-mutating GET that immediately mutes the topic; email scanners, prefetchers, and link-preview bots fetching the URL will silently mute topics — needs a confirmation step (GET page, POST mutation) or one-time token

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new GET route `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` (and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) and implements `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which *mutates state* by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` before returning `perform_show_response`. The unsubscribe URL is injected into notification emails (`unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`) and the email template renders it via `%{unsubscribe_link}`. This makes a state-changing action reachable via a plain GET link, which can be triggered by email link scanners/prefetchers or other automated fetches, causing silent changes to topic notification state without user confirmation/CSRF protection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe_link locale string now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url} but only send_notification_email passes it; other emails using add_unsubscribe_link: true will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument or render a broken link

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it always does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`, but `template_args` has no default `unsubscribe_url` (only `user_preferences_url` plus merged `@opts`). The diff updates `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` to pass `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` and updates the spec to pass `unsubscribe_url`, which suggests callers must now provide it. However, the diff does not show whether there are other call sites using `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url`, so the claim that other emails will definitely break is not directly verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client topic-unsubscribe route ignores params.slug, so slug-mismatched URLs silently load by id without server-side canonicalization

adjudication.rationale: While the Ember `topic-unsubscribe` route’s `model(params)` uses only `params.id` and does ignore `params.slug`, the diff *does* add server-side canonicalization for slug mismatches in `TopicsController#unsubscribe` via `if slugs_do_not_match ... redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url, status: 301`. Since the initial request to `/t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` hits Rails first, slug-mismatched URLs are not silently accepted without canonicalization as the finding claims.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HTML unsubscribe response renders the full topic :show template, so the unsubscribe confirmation is invisible without JS and no-JS/crawler users see no confirmation of the mute action

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the action mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and then calls `perform_show_response`. In `perform_show_response`, the HTML branch now explicitly does `render :show` (diff adds this), meaning the `/t/:id/unsubscribe` HTML response renders the normal topic `:show` template, not a dedicated unsubscribe confirmation page. The client-side Ember route/template (`topicUnsubscribe` + `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`) would only display if JS runs; with JS disabled (or for non-JS clients/crawlers), there is no unsubscribe confirmation UI rendered from the server response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicUser.find_by can return nil (user never visited topic or anonymous current_user), causing NoMethodError on tu.notification_level and a 500 crash in topics_controller unsubscribe action
Unsubscribe action mutates state (mutes topic) via plain GET with no confirmation, CSRF token, or intent authentication, allowing email scanners/prefetchers to silently unsubscribe or mute users

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a state-changing `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that toggles `TopicUser.notification_level` and `save!`s it, but it is wired up as a plain `GET` route (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`). The unsubscribe URL is also injected into notification emails (`unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` and server locale adds a clickable link). There is no confirmation step or token/intent check shown, and using GET avoids Rails’ CSRF protections typically applied to non-GET requests, so link prefetchers/email scanners could trigger the mutation silently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: dropdown-button.js.es6 buffer.push interpolates title unescaped, potential XSS if user-controlled content passed as title (pre-existing, P2)

adjudication.rationale:
In dropdown-button.js.es6 the code still concatenates `title` directly into an HTML string (`buffer.push("

" + title + "

")`) without escaping. The diff does not introduce this pattern (it existed before), but it keeps the unescaped interpolation in a code path that renders raw HTML. Whether this is an actual XSS depends on whether `title` can contain user-controlled HTML, which cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 301 redirect to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url uses potentially nil-slug URL and combined with nil TopicUser issue can crash on the redirect path

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` and then immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and assigns to `tu.notification_level` without handling `tu` being `nil` (no TopicUser row exists). That would raise a `NoMethodError` and is a real crash scenario introduced/exposed by this diff. The specific claim about the 301 redirect using a nil-slug URL isn’t clearly supported by the diff (the redirect uses `@topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url`, which is derived from the topic’s `url`), but the `TopicUser` nil dereference is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GET-prefetch traffic hitting the write path (tu.save! + MessageBus publish) causes DB write amplification from email-scanner crawls on every notification email sent

adjudication.rationale: The new unsubscribe endpoint is a GET route (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` in `config/routes.rb`) that performs a state-changing write: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` loads `TopicUser` and mutates `notification_level` then calls `tu.save!` (`app/controllers/topics_controller.rb`). This means any email link prefetcher/crawler that follows the unsubscribe URL added to notification emails (`unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` in `user_notifications.rb` and the new `unsubscribe_link` text in `server.en.yml`) can trigger unintended DB writes (and toggle state) just by fetching the link. The finding’s mention of MessageBus publish is not shown in this controller path, but the GET-causes-write amplification is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topics_controller.rb unsubscribe: TopicUser.find_by can return nil when user has no topic_users row, causing NoMethodError on tu.notification_level and a 500 error

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately dereferences `tu.notification_level` and assigns `tu.notification_level = ...` followed by `tu.save!`. If `find_by` returns `nil` (no existing `topic_users` row for that user/topic), this will raise `NoMethodError` and 500. The diff does not show any nil-guard or creation of a `TopicUser` record in this action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe action performs state mutation on GET request with no confirmation or CSRF/token protection, allowing email pre-fetchers/link scanners to silently change notification levels

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` routes, and implements `TopicsController#unsubscribe` that *mutates* `TopicUser.notification_level` (toggles regular/muted) and `tu.save!` on a GET request. There is no confirmation step or token/nonce in the URL; GET requests generally bypass CSRF protections and can be triggered by email link scanners/prefetchers, causing silent state changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe_link locale string now requires %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation, breaking other mailers that use add_unsubscribe_link without passing unsubscribe_url (e.g. digest/summary), raising I18n::MissingInterpolationVariable

adjudication.rationale: `config/locales/server.en.yml` changes `unsubscribe_link` to include `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb#html_part`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it unconditionally does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` and substitutes it, but `template_args` only contains `site_name`, `base_url`, and `user_preferences_url` unless callers pass more via opts. There is no default for `unsubscribe_url`, so any email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but without `unsubscribe_url:` will raise an interpolation error (e.g., `I18n::MissingInterpolationVariable/Argument`). The diff only updates one caller (`user_notifications.rb`) and one spec, leaving the API in a breaking state unless all other callers were updated elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe action does not handle anonymous/current_user == nil, causing nil deref on current_user.id; should redirect to login

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code assumes a logged-in user: it calls `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` and then `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)`. If `current_user` is `nil` (anonymous request), `current_user.id` will raise a `NoMethodError`. The diff also adds public GET routes for `.../unsubscribe` and skips `:check_xhr` for `:unsubscribe`, but does not add any guard/redirect to login, so the nil deref is a real exposed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: notification.html.erb emits respond_instructions footer twice, duplicating reply-by-email instructions in notification emails with context posts

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/email/notification.html.erb, when context_posts.present? the template renders a footer containing "%{respond_instructions}" inside the context_posts block, and then renders another footer with "%{respond_instructions}" again after the block (followed by "%{unsubscribe_link}"). This will duplicate the reply/response instructions in emails that include context posts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_show_response explicit render :show change may alter show action's HTML response for existing callers — verify it doesn't break existing topic page rendering

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `render :show` inside `perform_show_response` for `format.html` (TopicsController), but for the existing `show` action Rails would already render the `show` template by default. The explicit render is primarily needed because the new `unsubscribe` action calls `perform_show_response`; without it Rails would likely try to render an `unsubscribe` template. The finding’s claim that this may alter the `show` action’s HTML response for existing callers isn’t supported by the diff (it should be equivalent for `show`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicUser.find_by in unsubscribe action returns nil (e.g. category/tag watchers or first notification before TopicUser row exists), causing NoMethodError on tu.notification_level and a 500; needs a TopicUser.change/create fallback

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and assigns `tu.notification_level = ...` without checking for `tu` being nil. If no `TopicUser` row exists for that user/topic, this will raise `NoMethodError` and result in a 500. The diff shows no fallback creation path (e.g., `TopicUser.change`/`create`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe action doesn't handle logged-out users (expired email sessions): current_user is nil and TopicUser.find_by raises; missing login guard/redirect-to-login with return path

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the new action assumes a logged-in user: it calls `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` and then `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])`. If `current_user` is `nil` (e.g., logged-out/expired session from an email link), `current_user.id` will raise a `NoMethodError`. The diff shows no `ensure_logged_in`/guard/redirect in this action, so the finding is a real defect exposed by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe mutates state via GET with no CSRF token or confirmation, so email scanners/prefetchers can silently mute users, and toggle semantics (regular→muted) mean a prefetched click followed by real click re-enables notifications

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds state-changing GET endpoints (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) and the `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and saves (`tu.save!`) on a GET request, with no CSRF protection/confirmation shown. The unsubscribe link is also injected into notification emails (`unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` and server locale text includes a direct link), so email clients/scanners that prefetch URLs could trigger the mutation. Additionally, the action’s toggle logic (`> regular` -> regular else -> muted) means an accidental prefetch followed by a real user click can flip it back to regular, matching the finding’s “toggle semantics” concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: I18n.t('unsubscribe_link') interpolation now contains %{unsubscribe_url} but only send_notification_email passes it; other mailers with add_unsubscribe_link: true will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument or render broken links

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it unconditionally does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` and `template_args` defaults do not include `:unsubscribe_url` (only `site_name`, `base_url`, `user_preferences_url`, plus whatever the caller passes). This means any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also providing `unsubscribe_url` will now trigger missing interpolation / broken output; only `send_notification_email` and the updated spec shown in the diff pass `unsubscribe_url`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 route has no error handling on loadTopicView; deleted/permission-denied/network failures leave user on blank loading screen

adjudication.rationale: In the new `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, the `model(params)` hook returns `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...)` with no local rejection handling (`catch`/`error` action) in this route. The finding that failures could lead to a poor/undefined UX is grounded (no route-specific handling is added), but the specific outcome of a "blank loading screen" isn’t directly verifiable from the diff because Ember may handle/bubble route errors elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_show_response after unsubscribe renders show template with unvalidated params; TopicView.new may raise Discourse::NotFound/InvalidAccess not covered by unsubscribe action's handlers, yielding 500 instead of 404 for bad topic ids

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the action instantiates `@topic_view = TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` with no local rescue/handling, unlike `#show` which (per the diff context) has exception handling around its TopicView work. If `TopicView.new` raises (e.g., bad `topic_id` / access denied), this action will bubble the exception up, potentially producing an unhandled error instead of a controlled 404/redirect. This is a correctness/robustness issue introduced by the new action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Untested nil-TopicUser / anonymous-user path will crash: TopicUser.find_by returns nil for logged-in users who never interacted with the topic or when current_user is nil, causing tu.notification_level to raise NoMethodError and a 500

adjudication_records.issue_text: Untested state mutation on a GET request: unsubscribing is a write performed by a GET, so mail scanners/preview bots that prefetch links will silently mute the user's notifications

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `topics#unsubscribe` endpoint wired up via **GET** routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` in `config/routes.rb`). The controller action `unsubscribe` mutates state by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` (in `app/controllers/topics_controller.rb`). Because this write happens on a GET (and is linked from emails via `%{unsubscribe_url}` added to `unsubscribe_link` in `config/locales/server.en.yml` and passed as `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`), it can be triggered unintentionally by link prefetchers/scanners, silently altering a user’s notification settings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test for unsubscribe_link interpolation without unsubscribe_url: mailers setting add_unsubscribe_link: true without passing unsubscribe_url will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument or leak a literal %{unsubscribe_url} into emails; the only updated spec passes unsubscribe_url (happy path only)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the `unsubscribe_link` translation to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}` (config/locales/server.en.yml), and `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` always does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true (lib/email/message_builder.rb) without providing a default for `unsubscribe_url`. The updated spec only covers the happy path where `unsubscribe_url` is passed. While the diff updates one caller (`send_notification_email`) to pass `unsubscribe_url`, the diff does not prove all other potential callers do, so the finding is best treated as a specific missing edge-case test/guard rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Updated message_builder spec only verifies the List-Unsubscribe header, not the changed behavior (the per-topic URL in the substituted unsubscribe_link body/footer), so the test would pass even if the new link were dropped or mis-interpolated

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb`, the updated `message_with_unsubscribe` now passes `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"`, but the spec still only asserts the presence of the `List-Unsubscribe` header. Meanwhile the diff changes the `unsubscribe_link` translation in `config/locales/server.en.yml` to include a new per-topic interpolation `%{unsubscribe_url}`, and `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` still performs `%{unsubscribe_link}` substitution via `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`. Nothing in the spec verifies that the rendered HTML/footer actually includes (or correctly interpolates) the new per-topic URL, so the test would not catch regressions where the per-topic link is omitted or incorrectly inserted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No integration test for the changed perform_show_response HTML branch: render :show was added inside format.html, affecting the existing show action's HTML rendering path, and a regression breaks every full-page topic load

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `render :show` inside `perform_show_response`’s `format.html` block. From the diff, `perform_show_response` is invoked by `show` and the newly added `unsubscribe` action. For `show`, Rails would already render `show` by default, so this is not a clear behavior change, and the diff provides no evidence of a regression that would “break every full-page topic load.” If anything, forcing `render :show` appears intended to ensure the new `unsubscribe` action (which calls `perform_show_response`) renders the existing `show` HTML shell rather than looking for a non-existent `unsubscribe` server template.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests for the new frontend route/controller/template (routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6, controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6, templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs); acceptance/ES6 tests should cover PostStream.loadTopic loading, notificationReasonText being nulled, and page rendering; also the typo'd computed stopNotificiationsText is relied on by the template with no rendering test to catch a mismatch

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new frontend route/controller/template/view for topic unsubscribe (routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6, controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6, templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6) with nontrivial behavior (PostStream.loadTopicView in the route model hook and afterModel nulling details.notificationReasonText), but the diff shows no new acceptance/QUnit/ES6 tests covering this UI/route behavior (the only added test change is in spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb, unrelated to the new Ember route). The note about the typo’d computed property name is test-related: stopNotificiationsText is misspelled but is consistently referenced by the template ({{{stopNotificiationsText}}}) and controller, so it’s not a functional mismatch in this diff—rather, without rendering tests, such a mismatch wouldn’t be caught if introduced later.

Untested dropdown-button conditional-title behavior change: title header is now conditional on title being present and this.get('title') is no longer coerced, so undefined previously rendered

adjudication.rationale:
In `dropdown-button.js.es6`, `renderString` changed from always rendering `

` or an empty header; now it outputs no header at all). The diff does not include any new/updated tests covering this shared component behavior, so the finding about an untested behavior change is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing edge-case coverage of the unsubscribe level toggle semantics (watching/tracking → regular, regular → muted, watching users never drop to muted) — a spec matrix over all notification_levels is needed to pin intended semantics

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds new unsubscribe toggle logic in `TopicsController#unsubscribe`:
```rb
if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
  tu.notification_level = :regular
else
  tu.notification_level = :muted
end
```
This introduces nontrivial semantics across multiple notification levels (e.g., watching/tracking → regular; regular → muted; muted → muted). The diff does not add any specs exercising this behavior (only an email `MessageBuilder` spec change is present), so the finding about needing edge-case/spec-matrix coverage for the intended toggle semantics is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GET request in unsubscribe mutates state, allowing email scanners/link prefetchers to silently unsubscribe users without user intent; needs a confirmation page or signed token

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicsController#unsubscribe` and routes it via `get "t/:.../unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`. That action mutates state by toggling `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` on a GET request, and the email template now includes a direct `%{unsubscribe_url}` link (`server.en.yml` + `user_notifications.rb`). This enables unintended state changes if an email client/link scanner prefetches the URL, and there is no confirmation step or signed/tokenized URL shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Nil crash when TopicUser.find_by returns nil for anonymous users or logged-in users without a TopicUser record, causing NoMethodError on nil
matched_golden_ids: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying issue: TopicUser.find_by may return nil (e.g., no TopicUser record exists), and subsequent method calls on tu will raise a NoMethodError/nil pointer crash.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Business logic duplicated in controller instead of using TopicUser.change, skipping MessageBus publish and making level-selection policy unreusable

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff shows manual logic to find and update `TopicUser` (`tu = TopicUser.find_by...`, set `tu.notification_level`, then `tu.save!`) rather than using `TopicUser.change(...)`. The `TopicUser.change` method in the diff explicitly publishes a MessageBus event when `attrs[:notification_level]` is present (`MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, ...)`), but the controller path does not publish anything. This is a concrete, diff-grounded duplication/reuse issue and it bypasses the existing centralized policy/side effects (MessageBus publish, race handling).

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe_link translation always includes per-topic sentence with %{unsubscribe_url}, but unsubscribe_url is only passed from send_notification_email, so other mails render the literal placeholder or raise

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `unsubscribe_link` (server.en.yml) to always interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` renders this translation whenever `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true, but `MessageBuilder` does not provide a default `unsubscribe_url` in `@template_args` (it only merges whatever is passed in `@opts`). The diff updates `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` to pass `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` and updates one spec accordingly, but any other caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also supplying `unsubscribe_url` would now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` or render a broken placeholder. This is a real defect risk introduced by the translation change + lack of fallback in the builder.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_show_response rendering is overloaded so unsubscribe drags the full topic-view HTML response path; a dedicated template would be clearer

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the action builds a full `TopicView` and then calls `perform_show_response`. In `perform_show_response` the HTML branch now explicitly `render :show` and preloads `topic_view_serializer` (`store_preloaded("topic_#{@topic_view.topic.id}", ...)`). So the unsubscribe endpoint will follow the same full topic-view HTML response path as `show`, rather than having any dedicated server-side template/response tailored to the unsubscribe page. This is a diff-grounded architecture/clarity (and potentially payload/perf) concern, not a verifiable functional defect by itself given the SPA can still render the Ember `topic/unsubscribe` template after boot.

adjudication_records.issue_text: stopNotificiationsText is misspelled in controller and template, and the misspelling is now API—a future correctly spelled reference will render nothing

adjudication.rationale: In the new controller `topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, the computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (misspelled), and the new template `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` references the same misspelled name (`{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`), so nothing is broken right now. However, the typo is now part of the controller/template API surface for this route, making the codebase prone to future mistakes (a correctly spelled `stopNotificationsText` reference would indeed render nothing).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Large amount of unrelated reformatting (var→const, hash-rocket→symbol, whitespace churn) across five files mixed into the feature PR, polluting git blame and increasing merge conflicts

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly mixes feature work (new topic unsubscribe route/controller/template, new TopicsController#unsubscribe, new email unsubscribe_url) with broad stylistic/reformatting refactors in multiple existing files: e.g., `topic-from-params.js.es6` changes `function`/`var` to method syntax/`const` and rearranges declarations; `topic_user.rb` changes indentation, converts multi-line blocks to one-liners, and rewrites hash literal/update_all syntax; `app/views/email/notification.html.erb` is largely reindented and switches hash-rocket locals to keyword-style locals; `lib/email/message_builder.rb` reformats hashes and conditional assignment and tweaks whitespace. This kind of churn is unrelated to the unsubscribe feature and can indeed pollute blame and increase conflict surface, even though it’s not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No controller spec for topics#unsubscribe despite two routes added, leaving nil-crash and side-effect issues untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action and two new routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) with nontrivial behavior (redirect on slug mismatch, `TopicUser.find_by(...)` lookup, toggling `notification_level`, and saving). No controller/request spec is added for this new endpoint (the only spec change is in `email/message_builder_spec.rb`), so the new side effects and potential nil-case around `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` are not covered by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unauthenticated state-changing GET endpoint: GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe mutates notification level with no CSRF protection, no token, no confirmation, allowing any third party to silently mute/unmute a victim's topics via embedded links/images since GET requests carry cookies

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds GET routes `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` to `topics#unsubscribe` (config/routes.rb). The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action changes persisted state by toggling `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb). Because this state change is triggered via a GET request and there is no token/confirmation mechanism shown in the diff, it is vulnerable to CSRF-style triggering via cross-site GETs (e.g., embedded links/images) when a victim is logged in and cookies are sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Nil TopicUser crash: TopicUser.find_by for a user who has never interacted with the topic returns nil, and tu.notification_level then raises NoMethodError causing a 500 for fresh notification email recipients

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately dereferences `tu.notification_level` without any nil check. If no `TopicUser` row exists for that user/topic (e.g., a user who received an email but has never interacted with the topic), this will raise `NoMethodError` and 500 the unsubscribe request. The diff adds the unsubscribe URL into notification emails and routes it to this action, exposing this crash path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email client link prefetching (Outlook/Google preview scanners) silently unsubscribes users just by receiving the email; redesign needed with POST + confirmation page

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a side-effectful **GET** unsubscribe endpoint and links it from notification emails. Specifically, `config/routes.rb` maps `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `TopicsController#unsubscribe` mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` (toggling regular/muted) and `save!`s it. The email template now includes an unsubscribe link with `%{unsubscribe_url}` (`server.en.yml`, `user_notifications.rb` passes `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`). Because this action is triggered by a simple GET, automated email client link prefetch/preview scanning could unintentionally hit the URL and change notification state without user intent. This is a real behavioral/security defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_show_response now always renders show view for all callers, causing routing mismatch: server renders full topic page while Ember client hijacks to unsubscribe page, breaking for crawlers/no-JS users who see no confirmation

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `render :show` inside `perform_show_response` for `format.html`, but that does not create a “routing mismatch” for Ember: the new Ember route `topicUnsubscribe` is mapped to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`, and the Rails `unsubscribe` action intentionally calls `perform_show_response` so the standard topic `show` HTML (which boots the Ember app and includes preloaded topic JSON) is returned. The claim that this “breaks for crawlers/no-JS users” isn’t verifiable from the diff, and Discourse’s pattern is to serve the same `show` shell for different Ember routes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Ember route topic-unsubscribe declared at top level instead of nested under topic resource; nested URL /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe may conflict with existing topic post-number routes (/t/:slug/:topic_id/:post_number), possibly routing 'unsubscribe' as a post number

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a new Ember route at the top level (`this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' });`) and matching Rails routes, but the finding’s claimed conflict with an existing `/t/:slug/:topic_id/:post_number` (or similar) route cannot be verified from the provided diff because no such Ember or Rails route is shown here. Without seeing the pre-existing topic/post-number route definitions and their ordering/specificity, the asserted routing ambiguity is not demonstrably introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 301 permanent redirect from a mutating unsubscribe URL gets cached by browsers forever; should be 302/303

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, when `slugs_do_not_match` or the slug is blank, it issues `redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url, status: 301`. This is a permanent redirect on a route that exists specifically to change a user’s `TopicUser.notification_level` (stateful/toggling behavior). While the redirect happens before the mutation in that branch, using a 301 for this endpoint can be questioned because browsers may cache it long-term (e.g., from `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` to `/t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe`), which could be undesirable if canonical URLs change. The diff does show the 301; whether it’s strictly a “bug” is debatable, but it’s a concrete, actionable review concern about redirect semantics on this new unsubscribe flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe_link locale interpolates %{unsubscribe_url} unconditionally but only send_notification_email passes it, causing I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument or broken empty links in all other mailers (digest, signup, etc.) using add_unsubscribe_link

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}` unconditionally. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it always does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`; `template_args` only contains `site_name`, `base_url`, `user_preferences_url` plus whatever the caller passed. This diff updates only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` (and one spec) to pass `unsubscribe_url`, so any other existing caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but does not pass `unsubscribe_url` would now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` or render a bad link.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Typo stopNotificiationsText (double 'i') in topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 controller and template — functional only because both misspell identically

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` in the new controller (`topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`) and the template references `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` (same misspelling). This is a real typo/misnaming that doesn’t break functionality only because both sides match, but it’s a maintainability/clarity issue rather than a verifiable runtime defect in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Triple-stache {{{stopNotificiationsText}}} injects fancyTitle unescaped into HTML, potential stored XSS via topic title on the unsubscribe page

adjudication.rationale: In the new unsubscribe template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` renders a string as raw HTML. That string is built in the new controller `topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` via `I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications", { title: this.get("model.fancyTitle") })`, and the translation includes HTML (`{{title}}`). With triple-stache, any HTML present in `model.fancyTitle` will be injected unescaped into the DOM, creating an XSS risk if `fancyTitle` is not guaranteed to be escaped/sanitized.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic-unsubscribe frontend route does not restrict to logged-in users or verify ownership, failing unhandled for anonymous users or users without access

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `:unsubscribe` to `requires_login` in `TopicsController` and includes it in `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`, meaning the backend route is restricted to logged-in users (anonymous users should be blocked/redirected by the existing login filter). The finding’s claim that the frontend route “does not restrict to logged-in users” isn’t supported by the diff. The diff also doesn’t show any missing ownership/access verification in the frontend; access control would be enforced server-side via `TopicView.new(..., current_user)`/controller filters (not shown here), so the stated issue can’t be verified from the diff as written.
